entities.name: NF-kappa-B1 p105/p50
observations: The 768-residue query protein has 78.0% identity and 100% query coverage to reviewed Gallus gallus NF-kappa-B p105, E-value 0.
The sequence contains Pfam RHD_DNA_bind at residues 49-247 and RHD_dimer at 256-357, supporting an N-terminal Rel homology domain.
The sequence contains multiple C-terminal ankyrin-repeat hits spanning approximately residues 529-753, consistent with an NF-kappa-B1 p105 precursor.
A glycine-rich low-complexity segment occurs around residues 420-480 between the Rel homology region and ankyrin-repeat region.
The predicted molecular mass is 83.9 kDa, theoretical pI 5.48, and net charge at pH 7 is approximately -24.2.

No explicit catalytic reaction or cofactor annotation was retrieved; this is consistent with a regulatory transcription-factor precursor rather than a metabolic enzyme, but nonenzymatic status is not experimentally proven from sequence alone.

entities.name: Rel homology domain
observations: The query contains DNA-binding and dimerization components of the Rel homology domain, approximately residues 49-357.
This domain architecture supports sequence-specific NF-kappa-B DNA binding after generation of the p50-like N-terminal product.

entities.name: Ankyrin repeat region
observations: The query contains repeated ankyrin-domain signatures from approximately residues 529-753, matching the inhibitory/regulatory C-terminal region of NF-kappa-B1 p105.
The repeat-rich C terminus is expected to mediate protein interactions and cytoplasmic retention functions.

entities.name: Canonical NF-kappa-B signaling
observations: Reviewed NF-kappa-B1 homolog annotations associate the protein with canonical NF-kappa-B signal transduction, immune and inflammatory responses, transcriptional regulation, apoptosis, and cellular responses to TNF and lipopolysaccharide.
